transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get our weekly strategy meeting underway. We have a putative consumer class action on our hands regarding the automated invite-a-friend referral program and alleged misleading marketing. Before I issue our binding response strategy, I need to hear from each of you on your respective areas. Let's start with discovery status — where do we stand? And I also need to understand any client business constraints we should be aware of. Please go ahead with your updates.

transcript.text: Marisol, before you issue the binding strategy, I need to flag something critical on the arbitration front. While reconciling a late-produced onboarding export against the user-agreement database, I confirmed that exactly 312 of the 480 putative class members have executed agreements containing an arbitration provision. The remaining 168 do not have arbitration provisions. This means we can only compel arbitration for roughly 65% of the putative class — the other 168 would remain in litigation regardless. I have not yet incorporated this reconciliation into the formal arbitration analysis, but this materially affects any strategy that assumes we can sweep the entire class into arbitration.

transcript.text: Marisol, on the client business constraints front — during this week's business review, I confirmed that the client will keep the automated referral feature available, but will withdraw all referral-related marketing claims and complete that withdrawal within exactly 60 days, without admitting wrongdoing. The client has not yet put this position into the litigation strategy memo, so I want to make sure everyone here has it before you issue the binding strategy.

transcript.text: To summarize the discovery picture before you issue the binding strategy, Marisol: we have a split class on arbitration — 312 of 480 are covered by arbitration provisions, but 168 are not. Any strategy needs to account for that residual litigation group. And from Talia's update, the client is prepared to withdraw all referral-related marketing claims within 60 days while keeping the referral feature itself active, without admitting wrongdoing. That withdrawal could support the limited injunction approach the company has already proposed, but it won't resolve the claims of the 168 users outside arbitration. I'm ready to incorporate the reconciliation into the formal arbitration analysis as a follow-up commitment after you issue the strategy.

decisions.response_path: Dual-track: compel arbitration for covered users while litigating the non-covered residual group, paired with a limited injunction aligned to the client's marketing withdrawal.
decisions.arbitration_motion_scope: Only the 312 putative class members with executed arbitration provisions; the 168 without such provisions remain in litigation.
decisions.referral_marketing_claims_status: All referral-related marketing claims to be withdrawn.

commitments.detail: Incorporate the onboarding export reconciliation into the formal arbitration analysis, documenting the 312 covered / 168 uncovered split.
Prepare and file the arbitration motion scoped to the 312 users with executed arbitration provisions.
Draft the limited injunction proposal reflecting the client's commitment to withdraw all referral-related marketing claims within 60 days without admitting wrongdoing.
Coordinate with the client to formally document the marketing withdrawal position in the litigation strategy memo.
Develop litigation strategy for the 168 putative class members without arbitration provisions, including potential defenses and settlement posture for the residual group.
